- Bot Social conversations are 1:1; it does not list a FlyBot group. When a room gains a granted remote Bot (create-room, addParticipants, or 新建群聊 picking a friend's chat), the host fans out a `FLYBOT-ROOM-SHARE` envelope (`src/shared/room-share.js`) through `flybotSend` (`via: 'room-share'` for join/leave, `via: 'room'` for lines, `meta.roomId` set) so the Bot's owner's FlyBot can project it immediately — including a room with no chat lines yet. Receive is `rt.applyInboundRoomShare` (`origin: 'inbound-share'`, `recordInboundSharedRoom`), labelled **Shared room from \<inviter\>** with the room name stored. The envelope names the person who invited the Bot (#848): a human participant in the room when there is one, else the owner-level `ownerName` / `home` the social plugin keeps on that Bot's member record (read from `whoami`), so a group made from the sidebar no longer says `a friend`; a human participant whose name is this home's own label `You` (an owner with no name yet) is skipped for that owner-level name, so the far side never reads itself as the inviter (#883); a room projected in from an inbound share forwards its own `sharedFrom` inviter instead of this home's owner, so re-sharing never renames the person who invited it. A leave envelope, hide, or grant revoke marks it left/hidden. Which identity a projection records is the envelope's, not the transport's (#873): `applyInboundRoomShare` prefers `data.inviterName` / `inviterHome` / `inviterHandle` and keeps `event.from*` only as the fallback, so a room carried here by a Chief's Bot is still named after the person who invited it. The lookup matches the values a room already stores as well, so a projection recorded under the transport's identity before this fix resolves to the same room instead of forking a second `inbound-share` room; a line keeps its own `who`, or the sender when it names nobody, never the inviter. `reach()` allows a local member to message a remote that already sits in that room when `roomId` is on the send. Still not team mode.
